info.title: Goldsky API
info.description:
REST API for managing Goldsky resources — pipelines, subgraphs, and Edge endpoints. Create, deploy, monitor, and manage them programmatically.

For guides and reference, see the [Goldsky documentation](https://docs.goldsky.com) — including [Subgraphs](https://docs.goldsky.com/subgraphs/introduction) and [Pipelines](https://docs.goldsky.com/mirror/introduction).

## Authentication

Every request carries an API token as a bearer token:

```
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

Create one in the [Goldsky dashboard](https://app.goldsky.com/dashboard/settings/project) under project settings. A token is scoped to the project it was created in, so the project is never part of a request path.

Read operations need the Viewer role; writes need Editor.

## Errors

Errors are [RFC 9457 problem details](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457) served as `application/problem+json`:

```json
{
  "type": "https://api.goldsky.com/api/errors/subgraph-not-found",
  "title": "Subgraph not found",
  "status": 404,
  "detail": "No subgraph named 'my-subgraph' exists in this project.",
  "instance": "/api/v1/subgraphs/my-subgraph"
}
```

Branch on `type`, not on `title` or `detail` — the URI is stable, the prose is not. Every `type` dereferences to a human-readable page describing the cause and the fix; the full list lives at [api.goldsky.com/api/errors](https://api.goldsky.com/api/errors). Validation failures (400) add an `errors` array naming each offending field.

## Pagination

List endpoints that can return unbounded results — pipelines and subgraphs — page with `page_size` and `page_token`:

```
GET /api/v1/subgraphs?page_size=50
GET /api/v1/subgraphs?page_size=50&page_token=<pagination.next_page_token>
```

Keep following `pagination.next_page_token` until it comes back `null`. A page can hold fewer than `page_size` items and still have a next page, so treat a short page as "keep going", not as the end.

BearerAuth.description: API token generated from the [Goldsky Dashboard](https://app.goldsky.com/dashboard/settings/project). Pass as: Authorization: Bearer <token>

get.description: List all pipelines in the current project, ordered by name. Optionally filter by type. When `pagination.next_page_token` is non-null there are more results: pass it back as `page_token` to fetch the next page.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return. Defaults to 50.

parameters.name: page_token
parameters.description: The `pagination.next_page_token` from a previous response. Omit for the first page.

post.description: Create and deploy a new turbo pipeline. The pipeline name must be unique within the project. `name` may be provided at the top level or inside `definition.name` (top-level wins if both are present); at least one is required.

name.description: Pipeline name. Only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens are allowed. May be provided here or inside `definition.name`.

get.description: Get the details of a specific pipeline by name.

delete.description: Delete a pipeline by name. This action cannot be undone.

post.description: Validate a pipeline definition without deploying it. Accepts the same body shape as `POST /pipelines`, so a request that passes validation here can be submitted to `POST /pipelines` unchanged. `name` may be provided at the top level or inside `definition.name` (top-level wins if both are present); a missing, malformed, or reserved name is reported as a `{ field: "name" }` entry in `errors` rather than rejected as a bad request.

name.description: Pipeline name. Only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens are allowed. May be provided here or inside `definition.name`.

post.description: Deploy an ephemeral preview of a pipeline with all sinks replaced by a blackhole. The preview is automatically deleted after the TTL expires.

put.description: Pause a running pipeline. Can be resumed later.
Restart a pipeline. Optionally clear state to start fresh.

get.description: Retrieve execution logs for a pipeline. Supports cursor-based pagination and filtering.
Get the number of error-level log entries for a pipeline within a configurable time window (default: 6 hours, max: 7 days).
Get the current runtime status of a pipeline.
Get the internal state information of a pipeline. This endpoint proxies to the upstream Streamling API.

List all subgraphs in the current project, ordered by name then version. When `pagination.next_page_token` is non-null there are more results: pass it back as `page_token` to fetch the next page. A page can contain fewer than `page_size` items and still have a next page.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return. Defaults to 50.

parameters.name: page_token
parameters.description: The `pagination.next_page_token` from a previous response. Omit for the first page.

get.description: Get all tags and versions of a subgraph by name.
List the chains available for subgraph deployment.
Get a single subgraph tag or deployed version.

patch.description: Enable or disable the public/private GraphQL endpoints and set the description of a subgraph tag or deployed version. Only the fields you send are changed.

get.description: Retrieve indexing logs for a subgraph version (cursor-paginated).

put.description: Pause indexing for a deployed subgraph version. Can be resumed later. `version` must be a deployed version label, not a tag name — a tag is a moving pointer, so pause it by the version it targets.
Resume indexing for a paused subgraph version. `version` must be a deployed version label, not a tag name.

put.summary: Create or move a subgraph tag
put.description: Point a tag at a deployed subgraph version, creating the tag if it does not exist yet.

target_version.description: The deployed version the tag should point at.

delete.description: Delete a tag. The deployed version the tag pointed at is left untouched.
Delete a deployed subgraph version. Fails with 422 while the deployment is still referenced by a tag, pipeline or webhook.

put.description:
Deploy a compiled subgraph bundle as `name`/`version`.

Send `multipart/form-data` with a `bundle` file part — a zip of your `graph build` output. Bundles are limited to 50 MB compressed and 100 MB extracted.


Example: `curl -X PUT -H "authorization: Bearer $GOLDSKY_API_KEY" -F bundle=@build.zip -F description="My subgraph" https://api.goldsky.com/api/v1/subgraphs/my-subgraph/deployments/1.0.0`

schema.description: Send each option as an ordinary `multipart/form-data` field, e.g. `-F overwrite=0`. Fields appear below as `{ value }` because that is how a form field looks once parsed.

bundle.description: Zip of the compiled subgraph build directory (`graph build` output), sent as a file part.

overwrite.description: Deprecated. Send "0" or omit it — "1" is rejected. To replace a version, delete it and deploy again, or move a tag to it.

remove_graft.description: Set to "1" to strip the graft from the manifest before deploying.

skip_graft_validation.description: Set to "1" to skip validation of the graft base subgraph.

start_block.description: Block number to start indexing from.

graft_from.description: `name/version` of an existing subgraph in this project to graft from.

graph_node_shard.description: Advanced: pin the deployment to a specific indexing shard. Leave this unset unless Goldsky support asked you to set it.

requestBody.description: Send each option as an ordinary `multipart/form-data` field, e.g. `-F overwrite=0`. Fields appear below as `{ value }` because that is how a form field looks once parsed.

get.description: List all webhooks in the current project.

post.description: Stream row-level changes for a subgraph entity to a URL. Every delivery carries a `goldsky-webhook-secret` header; the secret is returned once in this response and is not retrievable afterwards.

name.description: A project-unique name for the webhook.

entity.description: The subgraph entity (table) to stream row changes from. Use the entities endpoint to list valid values.

webhook_url.description: The URL row changes are POSTed to.

secret.description: Sent as the `goldsky-webhook-secret` header on every delivery. Generated if omitted, and returned once in the create response.

delete.description: Delete a webhook by its project-unique name.

get.description: List the entities (tables) of a deployed subgraph version that a webhook can be attached to, with row counts and columns.
List the chains/networks available for Edge RPC endpoints.
List the datasets available through Edge Data endpoints.
List all Edge endpoints in the current project.

tags.name: Pipelines
tags.description: Create, read, and delete pipelines. A pipeline is identified by its name within the project.

tags.name: Pipeline Authoring
tags.description: Check a pipeline definition and see what it would produce, before creating anything. Neither endpoint touches an existing pipeline.

tags.name: Pipeline Lifecycle
tags.description: Pause, resume, and restart a running pipeline.

tags.name: Pipeline Status
tags.description: Query pipeline runtime status and per-source progress state.

tags.name: Pipeline Logs
tags.description: Retrieve pipeline execution logs and error counts.

tags.name: Subgraphs
tags.description: Read subgraphs and their versions. A subgraph is identified by `name`/`version`.

tags.name: Subgraph Deployments
tags.description: Deploy a compiled subgraph bundle as a new version, or remove a deployed one.

tags.name: Subgraph Tags
tags.description: Point a stable alias — `production`, say — at a specific version, so consumers keep one URL across deploys.

tags.name: Subgraph Lifecycle
tags.description: Pause and resume indexing, and update the settings of a deployed version.

tags.name: Subgraph Webhooks
tags.description: Stream row-level changes to a subgraph entity out to a URL. Webhooks are project-scoped and each one targets a single entity of a single subgraph version.

tags.name: Edge Endpoints
tags.description: Create and manage Edge endpoints — RPC and Data — including rate limits and allowed domains.

tags.name: Edge Lifecycle
tags.description: Pause and resume an endpoint. A paused endpoint rejects traffic but keeps its configuration and key.

tags.name: Edge API Keys
tags.description: Reveal the API key an Edge endpoint serves traffic under.

tags.name: Edge Metrics
tags.description: Request volume and error rates for an Edge endpoint.

tags.name: Catalogs
tags.description: What Goldsky supports: chains you can index a subgraph on, and the networks and datasets an Edge endpoint can be pointed at. Unauthenticated-safe reads that never change per project.
